name: CANtact Pro
one_line: Isolated dual-interface USB-to-CAN/CAN-FD adapter for vehicle network sniffing and injection, successor to the original open CANtact.
why_notable: cantact-hw 404 stars (2021-11-08), cantact-pro-fw 52 stars (2023-03-17). NOTE: the Crowd Supply survey reported this as discontinued/Not Available - status needs resolving before it is added.

name: panda
one_line: USB dongle tapping a car's CAN/CAN-FD/LIN buses (3x CAN, 2x LIN, 1x GMLAN) for sniffing, injecting and MITM of vehicle traffic; STM32H7-class MCU with ESP32 Wi-Fi.
why_notable: 1701 stars, last commit 2026-09-09. The most widely used open automotive CAN interface; also powers openpilot.

name: WiCAN Pro
one_line: ESP32-S3 OBD-II scanner with a dedicated OBD interpreter chip covering all legislated OBD-II protocols plus 3 CAN + 1 single-wire CAN, USB-C flashing, microSD logging, optional LTE/GPS.
why_notable: Higher tier of WiCAN; the page names car hacking as a use case but security framing is secondary to diagnostics.

name: CANtact v1.2
one_line: Open-source CAN-bus-to-USB interface (fork of the original CANtact) with USB-C and an RJ45-to-OBDII adapter for vehicle and industrial CAN networks.
why_notable: A second automotive CAN interface (alongside the Flipper CAN bus add-on above); a category with almost no existing DB coverage.

name: CANable 2.0 / CANable Pro
one_line: Isolated open-hardware USB-to-CAN adapter (CAN 2.0A/B, CAN-FD on v2) for sniffing and injecting CAN traffic; works with SocketCAN/Wireshark and cantact-app.
why_notable: canable2-fw 160 stars / canable-fw 260 stars, last firmware commit 2023-09-28. Descended from CANtact; one of the most cloned open CAN adapters.

name: CAN bus for Flipper Zero
one_line: MCP2515-based CAN bus add-on for Flipper Zero that reads, monitors, and resends/replays messages on a vehicle CAN network.
why_notable: Brings automotive CAN bus analysis to the Flipper Zero platform; the DB's automotive category currently has almost no coverage.

name: CANHack toolkit / CANPico
one_line: Bit-banging CAN protocol attack library (denial of service, error-frame injection and other data-link-layer attacks) in MicroPython firmware for the CANPico board, which includes a Pi Pico.
why_notable: 393 stars, last commit 2024-04-01. Reference toolkit for low-level CAN data-link attacks by a recognised CAN researcher.

name: CANBus Module for Flipper Zero
one_line: Flipper Zero add-on board that connects to a vehicle's CAN bus / OBD-II port for development, debugging and diagnostics (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: The catalog's only dedicated automotive CAN-bus interface, extending the Flipper Zero into vehicle diagnostics/analysis.
_possible_dupe_of: nRF24L01+ module for Flipper Zero (mousejack / 2.4 GHz)

name: WiCAN
one_line: ESP32-C3 wired/wireless CAN adapter (OBD-II or bare USB-CAN form factor) exposing CAN traffic over Wi-Fi/BLE with a web config UI; works with SavvyCAN, python-can, SocketCAN, RealDash.
why_notable: meatpiHQ/wican-fw 770 stars, last commit 2026-09-09. Returned independently by the GitHub and Crowd Supply searches.

name: Flipper Add-On: CANBus
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board for sniffing and injecting CAN bus traffic, with OBD2 scanning and UDS diagnostics on authorized vehicles.
why_notable: Adds automotive CAN bus sniff/inject/OBD2 capability to the Flipper Zero, a capability not covered by any existing Flipper add-on in the database.

name: hitager
one_line: Windows GUI + Arduino tool reading and writing 125kHz automotive immobiliser transponders (HiTag2, HiTag2 Extended, HiTag3, HiTag AES, HiTag Pro, VVDI Super Chip, BMW keys) via a PCF7991 base station.
why_notable: 87 stars, last commit 2023-01-09. Covered by Hackaday Oct 2023; one of very few open tools for car-key transponders, with no comparable alternative.

name: PiCCANTE
one_line: Firmware turning a Raspberry Pi Pico (or Pico 2/W) plus a CAN transceiver into a 3-channel CAN sniffer/injector with ELM327 emulation and SavvyCAN/SocketCAN compatibility.
why_notable: 93 stars, last commit 2026-01-26. Deliberately cheap alternative to proprietary CAN equipment.

name: EvilAppleJuice ESP32
one_line: firmware only, needs a generic ESP32 - spams BLE Continuity proximity-pairing adverts to trigger repeated iPhone pairing pop-ups.
why_notable: 2254 stars, last commit 2026-06-06. Presented at COSCUP 2025.

name: ChimeraBLE
one_line: firmware only, needs a generic ESP32 (also XIAO ESP32-C5 or Cardputer ADV) - full BLE GATT enumeration, HID report decoding, device cloning/emulation and BLE MITM proxying.
why_notable: 222 stars, last commit 2026-07-07. Host+peripheral+MITM in one tool, unlike the spam/jam-focused BLE projects.

name: Bluetooth Ducky
one_line: firmware only, needs a generic ESP32 - emulates a Bluetooth keyboard that auto-pairs and injects Ducky Script-style payloads, no physical USB access needed.
why_notable: 42 stars, last commit 2025-07-22.

name: BLE CTF
one_line: firmware only, needs a generic ESP32/S3/C6 - deliberately vulnerable BLE GATT server used as a hands-on CTF for learning BLE enumeration and exploitation.
why_notable: 776 stars, last commit 2026-08-07. De facto standard hands-on BLE training target.

name: OsmocomBB
one_line: Open baseband firmware for Calypso-chipset phones (used Motorola C118/C123/C139, ~$15 secondhand), turning one into a full open GSM stack for air-interface research.
why_notable: 331 stars, last commit 2026-06-17. Long-standing reference tool in GSM security research.

name: IMSI-catcher (Oros42)
one_line: software only, needs an RTL-SDR, HackRF or BladeRF - gr-gsm script that pulls IMSI/operator/country of nearby phones off GSM control channels.
why_notable: 4526 stars, last commit 2026-06-06. SOFTWARE, not a device - candidate for companion_software rather than its own record.

name: Android IMSI-Catcher Detector (AIMSICD)
one_line: software only, runs on an Android phone - detects fake base stations, StingRays and silent SMS via tower-consistency and signal checks. Some methods need root.
why_notable: 5417 stars, last commit 2026-09-04. SOFTWARE, not a device.

name: WiebeTech Forensic ComboDock v5
one_line: Dual-mode forensic drive dock that forces an explicit choice of write-blocked or read/write mode on power-up to prevent accidental writes to evidence drives.
why_notable: A forensic hardware write-blocker; the brief lists write blockers as in-scope forensics gear and the DB has no existing entries for one.

name: WiebeTech Drive eRazer
one_line: Stand-alone hardware drive wiper that erases SATA/IDE drives at native interface speed without needing a computer.
why_notable: A forensic drive-wiping appliance, filling out the forensics category alongside the ComboDock write-blocker above.

name: Rainbow Tables HDD
one_line: 2TB USB 3.0 hard drive preloaded with precomputed rainbow tables for A5/1, WPA-PSK, and MD5 password/hash cracking.
why_notable: It is a generic USB hard drive; its only differentiator is preloaded cracking data, not device hardware capability.

name: O.MG Malicious Cable Detector
one_line: USB inline device that uses side-channel power analysis (200,000 samples/sec) to detect known malicious USB cables, and doubles as a USB data blocker (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Defensive counterpart to O.MG-style malicious cables already tracked; no comparable detection device is currently in the database.

name: Keylogger USB Extension Cable
one_line: Hardware keylogger built into a USB extension cable body, with 16MB flash storage and timestamping, that records USB keyboard input.
why_notable: Same keylogger category as the AirDrive Forensic Keylogger already tracked, but in extension-cable form factor from a different vendor.

name: KeyGrabber
one_line: Inline hardware keylogger (PS/2, USB, or WiFi-exfiltrating variants) that records keystrokes transparently with no drivers or software needed.
why_notable: Long-running hardware keylogger product line, distinct from the AirDrive keylogger already tracked; includes a WiFi-exfiltration variant. Price shown is the low end of a $55-$120 range across models.

name: EvilCrow-Keylogger
one_line: Inline USB keylogger with microSD, ATmega32U4 for HID passthrough plus an ESP32-PICO for Wi-Fi exfiltration.
why_notable: 267 stars, last commit 2026-01-13. Returned independently by the GitHub and Tindie searches. Distinct hardware from the tracked AirDrive Forensic Keylogger.

name: PAW Protector
one_line: Inline USB-A adapter that blocks the data lines on a USB connection while passing 2.4A fast charging, to prevent juice-jacking on public USB ports.
why_notable: Defensive USB data-blocker device purpose-built against malicious public charging ports/cables.

name: Paw Detector – Malicious USB cables detector
one_line: Pocket USB-A adapter with an LED that lights steadily if a plugged-in cable contains a hidden keylogger or data-exfiltration circuit.
why_notable: Standalone hardware tool for detecting malicious/keylogging USB cables before use, presented at DEF CON 34.

name: USBKeylogger
one_line: Inline hardware keylogger between USB keyboard and host, capturing keystrokes to onboard flash and exfiltrating over Wi-Fi with AES-128 to ntfy.sh or a custom endpoint; invisible to host antivirus.
why_notable: 67 stars, last commit 2026-06-15. Gerbers published for compact and USB-hub form factors.

name: MACOBOX - Hardware Pentest Platform
one_line: All-in-one hardware pentesting platform for rapid connection, firmware dumping and analysis across multiple hardware interfaces.
why_notable: Top-end (~$11k) integrated hardware-hacking lab-in-a-box, the highest-priced item in the catalog and a distinct product tier from single-purpose tools like Bus Pirate or GreatFET.

name: ChipWhisperer - HuskyPlus
one_line: Side-channel analysis and fault-injection platform, an upgraded model above the existing ChipWhisperer-Husky.
why_notable: Higher-end successor to the ChipWhisperer-Husky already tracked, now in scope under the professional-gear price allowance.

name: AutoProber
one_line: Automation stack combining a GRBL CNC (e.g. Genmitsu 3018), a USB microscope and a networked oscilloscope (Siglent SDS1104X-E) with a 3D-printed toolhead to map a PCB, identify pins and run operator-approved pogo-probe measurements with scope-based safety cutoffs.
why_notable: 330 stars, last commit 2026-04-16. Flying-probe automation normally only found in closed commercial lab gear; needs an assembled CNC+scope+microscope stack, not a single purchase.

name: BugBlat miniSniffer 2
one_line: Compact, cross-platform USB protocol analyzer/sniffer for capturing and inspecting USB device traffic (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Dedicated low-cost USB bus analyzer, filling a gap between Cynthion-class USB reverse-engineering tools and basic sniffers.

name: Project Reboot: Hardware Audit Training Target
one_line: Deliberately vulnerable practice target with progressive UART, SPI, I2C and Bluetooth challenges for learning hardware-hacking techniques (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: A training target (not an attack tool itself) built specifically to practice the same interfaces (UART/SPI/I2C/BLE) that tools like the Bus Pirate attack.

name: FlatSat – DEFCON 34
one_line: RP2040-based training board preloaded with intentionally vulnerable firmware mimicking spacecraft systems, for practicing binary exploitation, SWD/UART hardware attacks, and LoRa telemetry analysis with an SDR.
why_notable: Purpose-built satellite-cybersecurity CTF hardware target presented at DEF CON 34; currently out of stock but a real catalog item with a listed price.

name: BRUSCHETTA Board
one_line: Multi-protocol UART/JTAG/I2C/SPI debugger and programmer supporting 1.8-5V target voltages.
why_notable: An all-in-one hardware-hacking debug probe from a known offensive-security researcher, comparable in role to Bus Pirate/Tigard but not yet tracked.

name: Pico Glitcher (fault-injection-library / Findus)
one_line: Raspberry Pi Pico voltage-glitching board (dual level shifters, transistors switching up to 66A, multiplexed 1.8/3.3/5V target power) with the Findus Python library, which can also drive ChipWhisperer Pro/Husky targets.
why_notable: 207 stars, last commit 2026-07-29. Sold assembled or as a kit via faultyhardware.de at EUR39-93. Also listed on Tindie as PicoGlitcher v3 at $59 - price discrepancy to resolve.

name: DigiLab for FlipperZero
one_line: Flipper Zero module for probing digital electronics: measures voltages, observes logic signals and reads sensor/module protocols on target hardware.
why_notable: Turns the Flipper Zero into a basic bench probe for voltage, logic-signal and protocol inspection during hardware audits.

name: Fire Weasel Board and Leash DIY Kit
one_line: Standalone 'Fire Weasel' carrier PCB and strap/leash sold alone for builders who already have their own CYD display and CC1101/NRF24/GPS modules; $48 unsoldered or $78 fully soldered and tested.
why_notable: Bare-PCB component (in scope under this project's DIY-kit rule) that forms the wiring backbone for the HaleHound build family; by itself it carries no radios, so its actual RF/NFC capability depends entirely on the CYD display and CC1101/NRF24/GPS modules the buyer supplies separately -- flagging borderline because the board alone does nothing.

name: SPIDriver
one_line: Dedicated SPI bus development/debug tool with an onboard screen, the SPI-protocol sibling to the I2CDriver (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Single-protocol SPI debug probe with live display, fills the same niche as I2CDriver but for SPI devices.

name: I2CDriver
one_line: Dedicated I2C bus development/debug tool with an onboard screen showing live bus activity for flashing and testing I2C devices.
why_notable: Single-protocol I2C debug probe with a live display, a narrower/cheaper alternative to multi-protocol tools like the Bus Pirate.

name: Lab401 Flashing Multi-tool for Proxmark & Chameleon
one_line: Small dongle for quickly reflashing/recovering Proxmark and Chameleon RFID devices (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Purpose-built recovery/flashing tool for two device families already tracked; marginal but distinct utility.

name: TermDriver 2
one_line: USB-to-serial adapter with an onboard screen that shows live serial traffic for debugging and monitoring headless/embedded systems.
why_notable: Serial debug adapter with an integrated display, filling a niche between a bare USB-UART cable and a full logic analyzer.

name: teensy4vfi
one_line: Firmware turning a Teensy 4.0/4.1 into a voltage fault-injection glitcher for bare-metal MCU/SoC research.
why_notable: 14 stars, last commit 2025-01-07. Author describes it as very early stage.

name: DirtyJTAG
one_line: Firmware turning $2 ST-Link v2 clones, STM32 blue/black pill boards, a Pi Pico or a Tang Nano 20k into a USB JTAG adapter for OpenOCD, UrJTAG, openFPGAloader and flashrom.
why_notable: 629 stars, last commit 2026-03-10.

name: CH552-DAPLink
one_line: CMSIS-DAP USB debug probe firmware and hardware for the sub-$1 CH552, giving SWD and JTAG access to ARM Cortex targets plus a virtual COM port.
why_notable: 52 stars, last commit 2025-06-02.

name: stm32f1-picopwner
one_line: Raspberry Pi Pico firmware implementing a published glitch-plus-flash-patch-breakpoint attack that bypasses STM32F1 read-out protection level 1 to dump protected flash.
why_notable: 322 stars, last commit 2024-04-01. Ready-to-run implementation of a published RDP bypass.

name: Flipper Zero SPI Adapter Board
one_line: Passive adapter board that breaks out the Flipper Zero's SPI pins so external SPI-capable modules (CC1101, NRF24, etc.) can be connected to it.
why_notable: Cheap enabling accessory for the SPI bus on Flipper Zero's GPIO header - required by JCMK's own SubGHz and NRF24 modules above; a genuine hardware-hacking/peripheral-bus item, not a generic cable.
mcu: n/a (passive adapter, no MCU or radio)

name: Airfrog
one_line: Coin-sized (16x28mm) wireless ARM debug co-processor on a $3 ESP32-C3-MINI-1: attaches to a target SWD header and exposes flash/RAM/peripherals over Wi-Fi instead of a wired cable.
why_notable: 60 stars, last commit 2025-09-07. Written in Rust; one of very few open wireless SWD adapters.

name: Curious Bolt
one_line: Pocket multitool combining a programmable crowbar voltage glitcher, an 8-channel logic analyzer and a differential power-analysis oscilloscope on one board; ships with an STM32F103 target and 4 challenges.
why_notable: 16 stars, last commit 2024-02-01. Vendor store page carried no price.

name: Steppenprobe
one_line: Open-hardware KiCad debug probe on an FTDI FT2232H providing simultaneous JTAG/SWD and UART/SWO over one USB-C connection, 14-pin Cortex connector, OpenOCD support.
why_notable: 44 stars, last commit 2024-07-15. DIY PCB build, no assembled price.

name: Cypherock EMFI Board
one_line: Open-hardware EMFI device converting USB power into a ~1kV pulse discharged through a hand-built EM probe, timed against a target MCU; ships with DUT boards for 7 MCU families used in crypto wallets.
why_notable: 27 stars, last commit 2024-01-06. Self-built PCB, no assembled price published.

name: HaleHound-CYD 3.5" Complete Unit Build
one_line: Hand-assembled ESP32 touchscreen (Hosyond 3.5" ST7796U CYD-style board) plus a CC1101 sub-GHz radio, NRF24L01+PA+LNA 2.4GHz radio, PN532 NFC/RFID reader and GPS module wired together, running custom firmware for WiFi deauth/evil-twin/captive-portal, BLE spoofing and BLE exploit replay (Airoha RACE CVE against headphones), NRF24 mousejack/2.4GHz sniffing, CC1101 sub-GHz replay/bruteforce/Flipper .sub playback, and MIFARE Classic NFC read/write/clone/emulate.
why_notable: Multi-radio (WiFi/BLE/sub-GHz/2.4GHz/NFC/GPS) pentest handheld built on a commodity 'Cheap Yellow Display' style ESP32 touchscreen (same class of board as the already-tracked ESP32 Cheap Yellow Display, though a different 3.5" Hosyond SKU, not the same product) with custom firmware self-authored by the seller (github.com/JesseCHale per the listing) -- not a rebrand of an existing named project such as Bruce or Marauder.

name: Fire Weasel and Leash PRO DIY Kit
one_line: DIY kit built around the community-designed 'Fire Weasel' carrier PCB (replaces hand-wiring): 3.5" exposed-SPI CYD, CC1101 sub-GHz + NRF24 2.4GHz radios, an ATGM336H GPS module with ceramic antenna, voltage boost/buck converters, and a 3D-printed case; seller states roughly a 45-minute build; no battery included.
why_notable: A redesigned, easier-to-solder version of the DIY HaleHound 3.5" kit using a purpose-built carrier board ('Fire Weasel', credited to community members BkBroiler and Hamspice/Midwest Gadgets) instead of a loose wiring harness; same firmware/radio capability as the other HaleHound kits, not a separate open-source project.

name: Biscuit Ultra
one_line: Same ESP32-C5 (dual-band WiFi 6 scanner) + ESP32-WROOM-32E (BLE/app link) chipset and firmware capability set as Biscuit Pro, in a larger enclosure: 3200mAh battery (~3x the Pro's runtime), dual external RP-SMA antenna connectors, a microSD slot for local/offline PCAP logging, and support for external 'node' devices to extend scan coverage across a wider area.
why_notable: (b) A genuinely different hardware model in the same family as the already-tracked 'Biscuit Pro,' NOT the same device under a new name and NOT just a firmware variant: different PCB/enclosure, bigger battery, external antenna connectors, SD card slot and multi-node support that the Pro lacks, while running the same underlying ESP32-C5/WROOM-32E firmware capability set. Reviewer note: this project's automated dedupe.py strips the word 'pro' when normalizing names, so 'Biscuit Pro' normalizes to 'biscuit' and would falsely substring-match 'Biscuit Ultra' -- confirm this stays a separate entry in Phase 2 rather than being auto-dropped as a duplicate.

name: DIY HaleHound 3.5" Kit
one_line: 3.5" version of the DIY HaleHound kit: exposed-SPI CYD touchscreen, 3D-printed case with embedded NTAG216, CC1101 + NRF24 'Cinder Ferret V2' companion board, and wiring harness; buyer solders and flashes it (no PN532 NFC reader or battery included).
why_notable: Larger-screen sibling of the 2.8" DIY kit with identical firmware and radio set, sold unassembled between the bare 2.8" kit and the fully-built complete unit in price.

name: DIY 2.8" HaleHound Kit
one_line: Unassembled kit: 2.8" CYD E32R28T exposed-SPI ESP32 touchscreen, 3D-printed case with an embedded NTAG216 tag, and a CC1101 sub-GHz + NRF24 2.4GHz 'Cinder Ferret V2' companion board with wiring harness; buyer solders and flashes the same multi-radio firmware used in the assembled HaleHound (no PN532 NFC reader or battery included).
why_notable: Same open multi-radio firmware/hardware design as the assembled HaleHound-CYD unit, sold as a bare-PCB/DIY kit (in scope under this project's DIY-kit rule) at a lower price; built on commodity CYD-style ESP32 hardware, not a rebrand of another named open-source project.

name: Feberis Pro
one_line: Flipper Zero add-on module adding RF/SubGHz, WiFi, BLE and GPS radios beyond the Flipper's stock hardware; USD price as shown on lab401.com's US store.
why_notable: Combines several wireless attack radios (RF, WiFi, BLE, GPS) into one Flipper Zero expansion board, claimed 10x over stock Flipper radio performance.

name: Bluetooth Nugget (ESP32S3)
one_line: ESP32-S3 board (dual-core successor to the USB Nugget) adding native BLE to the existing Wi-Fi monitor-mode and USB-HID keystroke-injection capability; screen and 6 buttons for on-device payload selection.
why_notable: Adds BLE attacks (demoed publicly sending pairing-request popup spam to nearby phones) to the open-source Nugget line, and is the base board for Retia's LoRa Meshtastic backpack add-on.

name: Newsheen Hacker Smart Cat Lamp Kit (pre-assembled)
one_line: ESP32-S3 board with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth built into a squishy cat-shaped desk-lamp enclosure; reflashable into an audio-reactive light, internet radio, or a Meshtastic/Meshcore/Reticulum mesh node.
why_notable: 'Newsheen' appears to be the OEM/brand of the underlying smart-lamp reference hardware; Retia resells it with open hacker firmware access to its ESP32-S3 (Wi-Fi/BT, upgradable to a LoRa mesh node) — the same 'known board plus community firmware' relationship called out for other entries, just in a lamp enclosure instead of a display or dev board; borderline since it ships and is marketed primarily as a lamp.

name: Solder Your Own Nugget Kit
one_line: Unassembled kit (PCB, SH1106 screen, 4 buttons, neopixel, 3D-printed case, plus a D1 Mini ESP8266 and an S2 Mini ESP32-S2 board) that the buyer solders into either a WiFi Nugget or a USB Nugget.
why_notable: Same open-source hardware/firmware as the WiFi Nugget and USB Nugget entries, just sold unassembled as a soldering-practice SKU — flagging as likely a duplicate device in different packaging rather than a distinct product.

name: Minino: IoT Multitool
one_line: Standalone handheld multitool that detects, sniffs and manipulates BLE, Zigbee, Thread, Matter and other IoT/sub-GHz protocols.
why_notable: Seller-described first dedicated multi-protocol IoT sniffing/manipulation tool, covering Zigbee/Thread/Matter which no other catalog device targets directly.

name: C5 LowKey - Flipper Zero
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO daughterboard with an ESP32-C5 built directly onto the PCB (no separate DevKit needed) running Marauder firmware for dual-band 2.4/5.8GHz WiFi analysis; onboard GPS module, microSD slot, protective enclosure. Does not include a Flipper Zero.
why_notable: A self-contained, assembled alternative to the DIY 'Marauder C5 Adapter' (below): same ESP32-C5 Marauder-on-Flipper concept but the radio chip is soldered to the board itself instead of requiring the buyer's own ESP32-C5-DevKitC-1.
has_screen: no, relies on Flipper Zero's screen
has_gps: yes, onboard GPS module + ceramic patch antenna included
has_battery: none onboard, powered via Flipper Zero GPIO
has_ext_antenna: GPS only (ceramic patch antenna); WiFi antenna is the C5's onboard chip antenna

name: Cinder Ferret V2
one_line: Second-generation Cinder Ferret companion board, adding an ATGM336H GPS module (1.25mm JST) alongside the existing CC1101 sub-GHz and NRF24 2.4GHz radios; shipped soldered with harnesses for all three modules.
why_notable: Same product family as the original Cinder Ferret with GPS added for wardriving; this is the companion board now shipped standard in the current HaleHound DIY kits, superseding the original Cinder Ferret.

name: Cinder Ferret V2.2 Double NRF
one_line: Variant of the Cinder Ferret V2 companion board with two NRF24L01 2.4GHz radios instead of one, alongside the CC1101 sub-GHz radio, for wider 2.4GHz spectrum coverage.
why_notable: Dual-NRF24 variant of the Cinder Ferret line, co-developed with 'Midwest Gadgets'; at the time of listing the seller states firmware support for the second radio was not yet released ('out shortly').

name: Cinder Ferret
one_line: Companion radio board that plugs into the HaleHound CYD build, combining a CC1101 sub-GHz transceiver and an NRF24L01 2.4GHz radio on one pre-soldered board with wiring harnesses.
why_notable: Bare add-on radio board (in scope under this project's DIY-kit rule) supplying the sub-GHz and 2.4GHz capability for the HaleHound firmware; sold standalone for builders upgrading or repairing an existing unit -- superseded by Cinder Ferret V2 in current kits.

name: Marauder C5 Adapter - Flipper Zero
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO adapter board (does not include the radio itself) that hosts a user-supplied, user-flashed ESP32-C5-DevKitC-1 to run Marauder for dual-band 2.4/5.8GHz WiFi analysis; onboard GPS module, microSD slot, enclosure.
why_notable: Cheaper bring-your-own-devkit version of the C5 LowKey (above) - same function, buyer must separately buy and flash an ESP32-C5-DevKitC-1. Fits the brief's DIY/bare-PCB-in-scope rule.
has_screen: no, relies on Flipper Zero's screen
has_gps: yes, onboard GPS module + ceramic patch antenna included
has_battery: none onboard, powered via Flipper Zero GPIO
has_ext_antenna: GPS only (ceramic patch antenna); WiFi antenna is the DevKitC-1's onboard chip antenna

name: Sneak32
one_line: Wi-Fi + BLE scanning firmware aimed at counter-surveillance: flags devices that keep reappearing near the user, to spot trackers or physical followers.
why_notable: 27 stars, last commit 2025-09-16. Defensive angle, tested on a XIAO ESP32-C3.

name: Hydra-ESP
one_line: firmware only, needs a generic ESP32 - multi-target deauth, AP cloning, deauth detector, BLE HID keystroke injection and Apple/Samsung/Google BLE pairing spam with a web UI.
why_notable: 203 stars, last commit 2026-07-18. Independently built, not a Marauder fork. Repo was renamed from ESP32-Deauther/HydraESP.

name: Gigabit Ethernet Tap
one_line: USB-powered passive single-port 10/100/1000BASE-T network tap with PoE pass-through, in a small metal case.
why_notable: Only Gigabit-capable Ethernet tap seen on the site; the taps already tracked (Throwing Star, Plunder Bug) are 10/100 only.

name: 10/100 FastE Switch Tap
one_line: USB-powered 5-port 10/100 Ethernet switch with port mirroring (port 1 to port 5) and PoE pass-through, used as a network tap.
why_notable: A switch-based network tap, mechanically distinct from the passive inline taps already tracked.

name: Glytch GPS Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: GPS add-on module for the WiFi Pineapple Pager that geotags captured networks/clients for wardriving (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Adds location-tagging to WiFi Pineapple Pager wardriving sessions, a real functional addition rather than a passive accessory.

name: Glytch Ethernet Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: Add-on module giving the WiFi Pineapple Pager wired Ethernet connectivity for LAN-based payloads.
why_notable: Capability-adding accessory for the already-tracked WiFi Pineapple Pager, enabling wired-network attack payloads.

name: PhanTap
one_line: OpenWrt package turning a small router into an inline traffic-silent network tap that masquerades as the victim device (bypassing 802.1X NAC) and tunnels a remote foothold out; runs on a GL.iNet GL-AR150.
why_notable: 626 stars, last commit 2025-10-06. Published NCC Group research; GL-AR150 is a different model from the tracked GL-AR300M.
